description: The bar chart illustrates the GLUE Performance (y-axis, ranging from approximately 85.5 to 89.5) of various fine-tuning methods (x-axis: Prefix, Adaptor, LoRA, BitFit, S₁-model, S₄-model, S₅-model) when applied to two sizes of the RoBERTa model — “base” (blue bars) and “large” (orange bars), as indicated in the legend. For most methods, the large model consistently outperforms the base model, with the largest performance gap observed in LoRA (base ~86.7, large ~89.1) and S₅-model (base ~87.1, large ~89.4). The Adaptor method shows a moderate gain from base to large (base ~85.3, large ~88.1), while BitFit exhibits a very low base performance (~85.1) but improves significantly with the large model (~87.7). The S₁-model shows nearly identical performance for both model sizes (~85.6), suggesting minimal benefit from scaling up in this configuration. The chart visually emphasizes that larger models generally yield higher GLUE scores across all fine-tuning strategies, with LoRA and S₅-model achieving the highest overall performance among the tested combinations.
